column1: # ACT_ID=ACT-POLYC-SELFHOST-WP001-DRIVER-TAKEOVER01-CORRECTION01
# ACT_PHASE=C3-EVIDENCE
# EVIDENCE_KIND=review-findings-repair
# TWO REVIEW-FINDING REPAIRS, MEASURED.
# An external review of the closed tree raised two source-level
# observations. BOTH WERE CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT, and both are
# test-oracle / predicate defects rather than production-compiler
# regressions. They are recorded here with the measurements that
# established them and the repairs that followed.
# FINDING 1 -- THE MACHO FILETYPE MAPPING WAS WRONG
# The differential runner's ClassifyArtifact() mapped the Mach-O
# filetypes as:
#     if (ft == 1) return CLASS_OBJECT;   // labelled MH_OBJECT
#     if (ft == 6) return CLASS_EXEC;     // labelled MH_EXECUTE
#     if (ft == 2) return CLASS_EXEC;     // labelled MH_EXECUTE
#     if (ft == 8) return CLASS_DYLIB;    // labelled MH_DYLIB
# APPLE'S ACTUAL VALUES, from the LOCAL SDK's loader.h:
#   /Library/Developer/CommandLineTools/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/
#     mach-o/loader.h
#   118: #define MH_OBJECT   0x1   relocatable object file
#   119: #define MH_EXECUTE  0x2   demand paged executable file
#   123: #define MH_DYLIB    0x6   dynamically bound shared library
#   125: #define MH_BUNDLE   0x8   dynamically bound bundle file
# So the mapping read MH_DYLIB (6) as an EXECUTABLE and MH_BUNDLE (8)
# as a DYLIB. The labels in the source were also wrong: the comment
# on the `ft == 6` line said MH_EXECUTE, and 6 is not MH_EXECUTE.
# MEASURED AGAINST THE REAL ARTIFACTS. The runner's own production
# compiler produced both kinds, and the filetype byte at offset 12 was
# read directly:
#   executable   -> 02 00 00 00   (MH_EXECUTE) -> the OLD mapping said EXEC (correct)
#   dylib        -> 06 00 00 00   (MH_DYLIB)   -> the OLD mapping said EXEC (WRONG)
#   $ file libcase.out.dylib
#   libcase.out.dylib: Mach-O 64-bit dynamically linked shared library arm64
# THE COMPOUNDING GAP: THE DYLIB ROUTE WAS NOT COVERED AT ALL.
# The frozen case table's D14 row was:
#   D14_dylib  %P -lib libtos.dylib input.HC -o case.out.o  0
# with expected class NONE (0). The dylib route writes lib<name>.dylib
# and does NOT write case.out.o, so the runner read NONE and the
# expectation matched: the case verified NOTHING. And even if the
# runner HAD looked at the dylib, the wrong mapping would have
# reported it as an EXECUTABLE.
# THE REPAIR:
#   R1  the filetype mapping is corrected to Apple's values:
#         1 -> OBJECT, 2 -> EXEC, 6 -> DYLIB, 8 -> DYLIB;
#   R2  the runner observes libcase.out.dylib, the file the dylib
#       route actually writes;
#   R3  the D14 row now expects DYLIB (4) and uses the -lib name
#       "case.out", so the route's real output is inspected.
# THE REPAIRED MEASUREMENT:
# THREE DEFECTS WERE FOUND AND REPAIRED WHILE MAKING THIS WORK, and
# they are recorded because each was a real defect in the test oracle:
#   D1  THE NB_SLASH_ASM REGION HAD NO TRAILING SPACE. Every other
#       slash region ends with a space (32) before its NUL; this one
#       ended with the NUL directly, so the rm command concatenated
#       the next path onto it:
#         rm -f .../case.out.s/tmp/.../g0/libcase.out.dylib
#       The dylib was therefore NEVER removed, and every case after
#       the dylib case observed a stale DYLIB. This was a PRE-EXISTING
#       latent defect in the runner; it was harmless while no case
#       produced a dylib.
#   D2  THE NB_TOTAL WAS ONE BYTE SHORT. The last byte written is at
#       index 424 (NB_VERDICT_DISAGREE + 8), so the array needs 425
#       bytes; NB_TOTAL was 424. The compiler lays the next static
#       buffer out at N_BUF + NB_TOTAL, so the final byte of the
#       array was the first byte of CMD_BUF.
#   D3  A LONG RUN OF BYTE-WRITES INTO A STATIC ARRAY IS
#       MISCOMPILED. The dylib slash path is 19 bytes written as one
#       run; the runtime bytes were measured by reading N_BUF back:
#       The last two bytes landed at the wrong offsets and the path
#       became "libcase.out.dylb". The 13-byte NB_SLASH_ASM region in
#       the same function was CORRECT, so the defect is a function of
#       the run's LENGTH. The write is now split into runs of at most
#       8 bytes, and the runtime bytes were re-measured to confirm
#       the placement.
#       This is the SAME CLASS of compiler defect the ACT already
#       documented for function-local static arrays; here it affects
#       a global static array with a long write run.
# FINDING 2 -- THE EMIT-LLVM CONFLICT PREDICATE WAS TOO BROAD
# The legacy C oracle (src/main.c at c92be049) tested the LLVM
# mutual-exclusion condition INSIDE an `if (args.emit_llvm)` guard:
#     if (args.emit_llvm) {
#         if (args.jit || args.repl || args.run ||
#             args.assemble_only || args.emit_object ||
#             args.emit_dylib || args.transpile || args.lsp)
#         { ...conflict... }
# The PolyC driver's WpDriverEmitLlvmConflict() flattened that nesting
# and DROPPED the outer guard: it returned 1 on seeing any of the
# conflicting options, whether or not --emit-llvm was requested.
# MEASURED DIRECTLY, with a probe against the REAL production driver
# subject, calling the REAL exported predicate on the REAL argv
# shapes:
#     shape                  legacy C oracle   PolyC driver   verdict
#     plain -c                    0                 1           DIVERGENT
#     plain -S                    0                 1           DIVERGENT
#     plain -transpile            0                 1           DIVERGENT
#     plain -lsp                  0                 1           DIVERGENT
#     plain -lib                  0                 1           DIVERGENT
#     --emit-llvm alone           0                 0           agrees
#     --emit-llvm + -c            1                 1           agrees
#     --emit-llvm + -S            1                 1           agrees
#     --emit-llvm + -jit          1                 1           agrees
#     --emit-llvm + -repl         1                 1           agrees
#     --emit-llvm + -transpile    1                 1           agrees
#     --emit-llvm + -lsp          1                 1           agrees
# The observable COMPILER behaviour was masked: the host renders the
# conflict diagnostic only on the LLVM route, and the status is
# consulted only when the action's own status is OK. The EXPORTED
# status was nevertheless wrong, and it is the PolyC driver's
# published semantic authority.
# THE RED WITNESS: tools/quality/wp001-driver-takeover01-conflict-red.HC
# is a COMPILED POLYC PROGRAM (F-POLYC-TOOLS). It links against the
# REAL production driver subject and calls the REAL exported predicate
# on the REAL argv shapes, comparing the driver's answer against the
# legacy C oracle's transcribed answer. The oracle's answer is itself
# checked against the case table, so the table and the transcription
# cannot drift apart unnoticed.
#   make wp001-takeover-conflict-red
#   BEFORE the repair: RED_EXIT_STATUS=1,
#     WP001_EMIT_LLVM_CONFLICT_RED=FIRED
#     5 mismatches, all of the "conflicting option WITHOUT --emit-llvm"
#     shapes:
#       CONFLICT_MISMATCH shape=plain_c        want=0 got=1
#       CONFLICT_MISMATCH shape=plain_S        want=0 got=1
#       CONFLICT_MISMATCH shape=plain_transpile want=0 got=1
#       CONFLICT_MISMATCH shape=plain_lsp      want=0 got=1
#       CONFLICT_MISMATCH shape=plain_lib      want=0 got=1
#   AFTER the repair:  RED_EXIT_STATUS=0,
#     WP001_EMIT_LLVM_CONFLICT_RED=NOT_FIRED
# THE REPAIR: WpDriverEmitLlvmConflict() now FIRST establishes that
# --emit-llvm was requested, and only then looks for a conflicting
# option. The legacy nesting is restored.
# A PRE-EXISTING DEFECT FOUND WHILE RE-MEASURING (RESIDUE, F11)
# While re-running the 30-case differential, the D25_transpile case
# disagreed under a DEBUG (AddressSanitizer) build of the compiler.
# The disagreement was NOT a semantic difference between G0 and G1:
# BOTH generations aborted with the same status. The abort was an
# AddressSanitizer report in the LEGACY C LEXER:
#   ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow
#     #0 lexNextChar+0x188
#     #1 lexCore
#     #2 lex
#     #3 lexToken
# THE DEFECT IS PRE-EXISTING AND NOT CAUSED BY EITHER REPAIR. It was
# measured by stashing EVERY change of this repair sequence and
# rebuilding the PRISTINE close tree (16a7fc93):
#   git stash push -u
#   build the selector-OFF compiler with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
#   run: hcc --install-dir=<prefix> -transpile input.HC
#   -> AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow in lexNextChar
#   git stash pop
# The pristine tree reproduces the identical abort at the identical
# frame, so the defect belongs to the tree this ACT inherited and not
# to the repair. It is in the LEGACY C LEXER, which this ACT does not
# touch.
# IT IS NOT OBSERVABLE IN THE CANONICAL BUILD. The repository's
# canonical build type is Release (Makefile: BUILD_TYPE ?= Release),
# and the Release build does not abort: the D25 case exits 0 in BOTH
# generations and the differential is 30/30 AGREE. The abort is an
# AddressSanitizer-only report on a build configuration the canonical
# gates do not use.
#   RESIDUE_CLASS=P2
#   RESIDUE_DISPOSITION=DEFERRED
# The repair of the legacy C lexer's end-of-file overread is OUTSIDE
# this ACT's authorized scope: the ACT's subject is the WP-001 driver
# route authority, and the legacy C lexer is retained deliberately as
# the selector-OFF oracle. It is recorded here, not silently fixed
# (F11), and not silently dropped.
# THE DIFFERENTIAL INVOCATION RECIPE
# The runner takes the case table VERBATIM and PREPENDS the compiler
# path itself, so the table's %P placeholder must be expanded to the
# compiler's --install-dir option BEFORE the table is handed to the
# runner. The recipe, measured on this tree:
#   1. build G0 (selector OFF) and G1 (selector ON) from the SAME
#      working-tree state, with CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release;
#   2. create the working directories <work>/g0 and <work>/g1, each
#      holding input.HC, broken.HC and other.HC (the fixtures the case
#      table names);
#   3. expand the placeholder:
#        sed "s|%P|--install-dir=<prefix>|g" cases.tsv > cases-subst.tsv
#   4. run:
#        ./build/wp001-takeover-diff cases-subst.tsv <G0> <G1> <work>
# The compiler paths MUST BE ABSOLUTE: the runner `cd`s into the
# per-generation working directory before invoking the compiler, so a
# relative path is not found (exit 127) and every case disagrees.
# THE MEASURED RESULT ON THE REPAIRED TREE:
#   D14_dylib        G0=0/DYLIB  G1=0/DYLIB  AGREE
#   D02_executable   G0=0/EXEC   G1=0/EXEC   AGREE
#   CASES=30 ; DISAGREE=0 ; DIFFERENTIAL=PASS
# CONSERVATION AFTER BOTH REPAIRS
#   PARSER            376/376 over 90 blocks, 0 failed lines,
#                     assertion-sequence MD5
#                     IDENTICAL to the entry baseline
#   LEXER07           89/89, 0 fail
#   LEXER08           45/45, 0 fail
#   LEXER09           23/23, 0 fail
#   G0/G1 DIFFERENTIAL 30 cases, 0 disagreements, DIFFERENTIAL=PASS
#   CONFLICT RED      NOT_FIRED, exit 0
#   GATE_FAST         VERDICT=PASS
#   BOOTSTRAP         the stage0 compiler compiles the repaired PolyC
#                     driver subject to a BYTE-IDENTICAL object
# WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the production compiler's SEMANTICS. The
# conflict predicate's OBSERVABLE behaviour was already correct
# (masked by the host's route-scoped rendering), and the Mach-O
# mapping lives in the TEST ORACLE, not in the compiler. The WP-001
# migration itself -- the route decision in the compiled PolyC
# driver -- is untouched by both repairs.
#   D02_executable   G0=0/EXEC   G1=0/EXEC   AGREE
#   D13_dash_filename G0=0/NONE  G1=0/NONE  AGREE
#   D14_dylib        G0=0/DYLIB  G1=0/DYLIB  AGREE
#   CASES=30 ; DISAGREE=0 ; DIFFERENTIAL=PASS
